(2) Each evaluation's JSON decode spent most of its time in JSONValue building coding paths for thrown type mismatches; KubeJSON.decoder now marks its source as typed JSON (release benchmark on the drifted 872-pod list: 158 -> 74 ms; a full JSONValue tree 445 -> 165 ms). The split between the fixes and the cleaner cluster was not measured separately.

soak-5.note: 60 minutes, valid (connected and visible every minute, app alive at the end), leaks at the end. PASS: footprintGrowthMB 0.0, leaks 0, threads +0, fds -1, slope negative. FAILS footprintMB: 277 against 200, so the M4a soak gate stays OPEN. Every minute sample above 200 MB (9 of 60) lands on a navigation cycle; between cycles the footprint is 160-170 MB. A per-second footprint breakdown through one cycle (.build/perf/soak-peak, 20:10) shows what the peak is: 'Owned physical footprint (unmapped) (graphics)' jumps from under 1 MB to 97 MB for about one second at each tab open and at the split (the window-server transient of overlapping windows that M4a recorded), on top of a working set that peaks at about 204 MB while the cycle's four tabs and split are open (Malloc Small 110 -> 150 MB) and returns to about 183 MB after the cycle. cpuAvgPct 5.95 includes the 10 lines/s log follow, the Deck Terminal watch and the cycle.

tabs-20.note: P2 Allocations check (ARCHITECTURE-MAC 12.3.5, generation marks in CLI form): perf/scenarios/tabs-20.json opens 20 tabs one after another (ConfigMaps 2,000 rows, Deployments, Pods, cluster overviews, the Fleet over 3 clusters) and closes them every 90 s; a memgraph after each round (leaks --outputGraph) is compared with the next (heap -s, heap --diffFrom, malloc_history with MallocStackLogging). Before the fix: +50 dispatch_source_t per round, each a cancelled Task.sleep(for: .seconds(3600)) of a store consumer whose one-hour dispatch timer stays armed until it fires; fixed with Task.waitUntilCancelled (dispatch sources per round after the fix: 132, 133, 132, 130). Remaining per-round growth, about 0.75 MB of heap per 20 tabs with leaks 0 and flat view instance counts, is inside the frameworks: SwiftUI GlassContainer dictionary capacity (about 0.4 MB), AppKit's computed-property KVO dependencies (NSKeyValueDependency and its contexts and blocks, +1.9k objects, about 0.3 MB, from NSScrollView layout, safe-area and glass-context getters), and +48 __NSObserver per round, about 23 of them from SwiftUI's AppKitTextInputSuggestionsBridge.setUpNotifications(window:) each time our toolbar search field (ToolbarSearchField, Wheelhouse/App/PaneVisibility.swift) is moved back into the toolbar on a tab switch (a SwiftUI bug that our toolbar triggers; an NSSearchField representable would avoid it and is left for 1.1). Persistent growth after close is therefore NOT 0.
